input.quote: This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000
input.rationale: Section 22.4 is asymmetric and fails the fallback. M&I may "freely assign" in any merger, reorganization or sale of assets, stock or securities (and to a successor of its Data Services division), whereas Customer's carve-out reaches only a merger in which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000; an acquisition or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets to any other successor needs consent. Neither party's successor assignment carries a written-notice mechanic. The consent requirement for other assignments and the "not be unreasonably withheld" standard are already met. We therefore target the fallback: a mutual successor right on written notice, achieved by broadening Customer's carve-out and removing "freely". We did not pursue preferred (affiliate carve-out, no Vendor assignment without our consent, competitor bar), which would require deleting M&I's assignment rights and collateral rewrites. Separately, Section 21.11.B gives M&I no termination right on Customer's Change in Control ("M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement"), though it caps M&I's service obligation at pre-change volumes plus 25%; Section 11.3 (Following Change in Control of Customer) is redacted, and the Section 11.1 carve-out for 11.3 terminations indicates it is a Customer right, so no walk-away trigger is flagged.

proposal.summary: Give Customer a genuine successor assignment carve-out and require written notice for both parties' successor assignments
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our fallback position is a mutual right to assign to a successor on written notice, with consent (not unreasonably withheld) for other assignments. We broadened Customer's carve-out from mergers with $100,000,000 financial institutions to any successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made both parties' successor assignments subject to written notice.
